title: Players on New Teams
brief: Which players changed teams, and is their value likely to rise or fall in the new usage and minutes picture? It must reflect that new-team players often dip in year one unless minutes rise, and flag ripple effects on teammates.
summary: Expect players on new teams to dip in year one unless their minutes rise. In our auction, pay full value only where the move adds minutes or a clear role, as with Naz Reid, Kel'el Ware and Paul George. Bid the low end of the range for stars joining crowded teams (Jaylen Brown, LeBron James, Kawhi Leonard), leave most deep movers to waivers, and watch the first 15 games on reshuffled rosters before spending FAB.

paragraphs.text: The notes agree on the starting point. When a good player moves, his production usually dips. Stars lose some value too, and growing pains are common in the first season.

For our auction this means one simple rule. When a mover has a price range, bid at the low end unless his minutes clearly go up. Jaylen Brown is the clearest case. Experts put him in the 40s for a smaller role in Philadelphia, so the 29 USD our league paid last season looks too high. LeBron James fits about 15 to 20 USD, not the 22 USD he went for last year. For Kawhi Leonard, bid in the low to mid 20s and let someone else pay ESPN prices.

sections.heading: The exception: more minutes or a steadier role

paragraphs.text: More minutes on the new team can offset the adjustment hit. A player who moves to a deeper team can even lose usage and still gain value, because his minutes and role get more stable. One note also says usage and minutes changes on a new team can raise a player's value a lot. Judge last season's rank in light of his old role, teammates and minutes.

These are the movers where the role grows. Naz Reid goes to Charlotte. The market prices him far below his 15 to 20 USD value, so target him if he plays 31 or more minutes. Kel'el Ware may start at power forward in Milwaukee, and experts see top 40 upside at 30 minutes. Paul George becomes Boston's number two option. Experts expect a top 40 per game finish, so paying up to about 12 USD is fine. Giannis Antetokounmpo's assists could rise because Miami is short on ball handlers. Walker Kessler becomes the Lakers' starting center, but experts still want you to stop near 15 USD.

Other moves shrink the role, and the price should fall with it. Miles Bridges may lose shots in Phoenix next to Booker, Green and Brooks. DeMar DeRozan projects for about 29 minutes off the bench in Denver. Nikola Vučević is a backup in Orlando after going for 17 USD here last season. John Collins lost his Clippers starting job and needs about 31 minutes in Detroit. Keep each of them in the 1 to 3 USD range.

The notes split on how much a new role can help. One side says a usage and minutes change on a new team can raise a player's value a lot, and that losing usage on a deeper team can still add value through steadier minutes. The other side warns that going from a good team to a bad team does not automatically mean bigger numbers, because usage can rise while playing time falls. In practice, do not pay extra for a usage bump on a weak team until the minutes show up. Randle in Brooklyn is a good test: check that he gets both about 30% usage and about 32 minutes.

Teams with heavy roster turnover tend to be rocky in year one. It goes better when the core stays together, and adding stars to existing stars has been choppy at first. Coaches may try a rotation for about 15 games and then reverse it, so back-end players on these teams are uncertain. Do not spend more than 1 USD on bench pieces from these teams. Use FAB on them only after the rotation settles.

Moves ripple out to new teammates and to the team the player left. The Giannis trade reshapes both Miami and Milwaukee. In Milwaukee, Tyler Herro shares a crowded backcourt with Rollins, Ware hopes to start next to Turner, and Jaime Jaquez Jr. and Kasparas Jakučionis fight for minutes. In Miami, Bobby Portis plays behind Adebayo and Giannis, while Tim Hardaway Jr. and Klay Thompson compete for guard minutes.

Philadelphia is the stars-on-stars case. LeBron and Brown join Embiid and Maxey. Check Brown's usage when Embiid and LeBron both play, and whether LeBron at point guard pushes his assists toward 8. Anfernee Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope only matter if injuries or rest days push their minutes up. Paul George, who left Philadelphia, gains the most from the trade.

The Kawhi trade has two sides. Kawhi takes Brandon Ingram's spot in Toronto. Ingram is out with an Achilles injury, which opens a window for Clippers teammates. Rui Hachimura replaces Collins at power forward and may get more shots. Max Strus could start and get back to about 4 assists. Gradey Dick only matters if the long trial rotations give him steady minutes. Elsewhere, LaMelo Ball must keep 7 to 8 assists next to Edwards in Minnesota, and Grayson Allen gets a short-term role in Charlotte while Knueppel is out.

At the auction, plan to pay full price for Giannis (about 60 USD or more). Stop near the low end of 28 to 32 USD for LaMelo. Good value at price: Naz Reid, Ware, Paul George, Herro at about 12 to 16 USD, Randle as a mid-priced starter, and Norman Powell at 7 to 9 USD. Brandon Ingram is a few-dollar stash for one of our 4 IL slots.

Do not pay last season's price for movers who lost their role. Ja Morant went for 17 USD and is now a 3 to 5 USD flyer. Deandre Ayton went for 9 USD and now ranks outside our 144-player pool. Santi Aldama, Bennedict Mathurin and Anfernee Simons were all drafted here last season and now belong on waivers.

In the first two to three weeks, check minutes before usage. Yahoo and ESPN split on several movers. Morant projects for 5.7 assists on Yahoo against 7.2 on ESPN, and Mathurin for a bench role against his old workload. Early games will settle these splits, so save FAB and the 6 weekly adds for movers who clear their minutes threshold. Before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline, watch for trade talk around Herro, Powell and Jaquez.
